title: Must, Don't Have To, Without & なさい
description: なければならない / なくてはいけない (must), なくてもいい (don't have to), ないで (without doing), and commands with なさい.

points.title: 〜なければいけない / ならない: must, have to
points.summary: ない-form → drop い + ければ + いけない/ならない. Literally 'if you don't, it won't do'. Casual: 〜なきゃ.
points.body:
**Formation:** ない-form, drop い, add **ければ** + いけない / ならない:
- 行かない → 行か**なければ**いけません
- 食べない → 食べ**なければ**なりません
- しない → し**なければ**…, 来ない → 来**なければ**…

**いけない vs ならない:**
- **いけない**: more personal or situational, common in speech ('I have to').
- **ならない**: more formal and general (rules, laws, social obligations), common in writing.

In practice they're often interchangeable.

**Casual forms:**
- 〜**なきゃ**（いけない）: 行かなきゃ！ (The ending is often dropped.)
- 〜**ないと**（いけない）: 行かないと.

Don't confuse it with **〜なくてもいい** = 'don't have to'.
examples: {明日|あした}までにレポートを{出|だ}さなければなりません。
I have to hand in the report by tomorrow.
{毎日|まいにち}{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}まなければいけません。
I must take medicine every day.
もう{帰|かえ}らなきゃ。
I've got to go home now.

points.title: 〜なくてはいけない / ならない: must, have to
points.summary: ない-form → drop い + くては + いけない/ならない. It means the same as なければ. Casual: 〜なくちゃ.
points.body:
**Formation:** ない-form, drop い, add **くては** + いけない / ならない:
- 行かない → 行か**なくては**いけません
- 勉強しない → 勉強し**なくては**なりません

The meaning is the same as 〜なければいけない. Some speakers feel なくては is slightly more conversational or personal, but they're interchangeable at N4.

**Casual form:** 〜**なくちゃ**（いけない）: もう寝なくちゃ (I've got to sleep). This is the contraction of なくては, just as 〜ちゃ is of 〜ては.

**Structure check:** なくて + は + いけない. Leaving out は (なくていけない) is wrong.
examples: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しなくてはいけません。
You have to practise every day.
{宿題|しゅくだい}をしなくてはなりません。
I must do my homework.
もう{行|い}かなくちゃ。
I have to go now.

points.title: 〜なくてもいい: don't have to
points.summary: ない-form → drop い + くてもいい(です) = 'it's okay not to …'. It's the answer to 'must I?' when the answer is no. Formal: なくてもかまいません.
points.body:
**Formation:** ない-form, drop い, add **くてもいい**:
- 来ない → 来**なくてもいい**です (you don't have to come)
- 書かない → 書か**なくてもかまいません** (more formal)

It literally means 'even if you don't …, it's fine'.

**Typical exchange:**
- A: 全部食べなければいけませんか。 (Must I eat it all?)
- B: いいえ、食べ**なくてもいいです**よ。 (No, you don't have to.)

**Contrast:**
- 〜てもいい = may (permission)
- 〜なくてもいい = don't have to (no obligation)
- 〜てはいけない = must not
- 〜なければいけない = must
examples: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みだから、{早|はや}く{起|お}きなくてもいいです。
Tomorrow's a holiday, so I don't have to get up early.
{名前|なまえ}は{書|か}かなくてもかまいません。
You don't have to write your name.

points.title: 〜ないで: without doing / instead of
points.summary: ない-form + で = 'without doing A, (do) B'. It's different from なくて, which gives a reason.
points.body:
**ない-form + で** links two actions: B is done **without doing A**:
- 朝ご飯を食べ**ないで**学校に行きました (I went to school without eating breakfast).
- 辞書を使わ**ないで**読んでください (please read it without using a dictionary).

It also means **'instead of'**: バスに乗ら**ないで**、歩いて行きました (I walked instead of taking the bus).

**ないで vs なくて (a common trap):**
- **ないで** = without / instead of. It describes the manner of the action.
- **なくて** = because … not. It gives a **reason**: 宿題が終わら**なくて**、寝られませんでした (I couldn't sleep because I hadn't finished my homework).

At the end of a request it forms ないでください ('please don't', N5).
examples: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べないで{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}きました。
I went to school without eating breakfast.
{傘|かさ}を{持|も}たないで{出|で}かけました。
I went out without an umbrella.
バスに{乗|の}らないで、{歩|ある}いて{帰|かえ}りました。
Instead of taking the bus, I walked home.

points.title: 〜なさい: do it! (command)
points.summary: ます-stem + なさい is a firm but not rude command. It's used from parents to children, teachers to students, and in test instructions.
points.body:
**Formation:** ます-stem + **なさい**: 寝**なさい**, 食べ**なさい**, 勉強し**なさい**, 来 (き) **なさい**.

**Who uses it:** people with clear authority over the listener, such as parents to children, teachers to students, and **exam instructions** (正しいものを選び**なさい**: choose the correct one).

**Never** use it toward superiors or strangers. It sounds bossy. Politely, use 〜てください.

In casual speech, なさい is sometimes shortened to **な**: 早く寝**な** (ます-stem + な). Don't confuse that with the blunt prohibition 'dictionary form + な' (寝る**な** = don't sleep!).

It comes from the honorific verb なさる ('to do'), but as a command it's not respectful at all.
examples: {早|はや}く{寝|ね}なさい。
Go to bed now.
{宿題|しゅくだい}をしなさい。
Do your homework.
{正|ただ}しいものを{一|ひと}つ{選|えら}びなさい。
Choose the one correct answer. (exam instruction)

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}までにレポートを{出|だ}さ（　）なりません。
notes: なくれば isn't a form.
なくてもなりません is contradictory. なくてもいい = 'don't have to'.
The い of ない changes to ければ: なければ, not なけば.
questions.translation: I have to hand in the report by tomorrow.

questions.prompt: {毎日|まいにち}この{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}ま（　）いけません。
questions.explanation: 飲まない → 飲ま**なければ**いけません ('must take').
notes: なくれば isn't a form.
なくてもいけません isn't a pattern. なくてもいい = 'don't have to'.
Drop the い of ない before ければ: なければ.
questions.translation: I have to take this medicine every day.

questions.prompt: あ、もう9{時|じ}だ！{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}ら（　）。
questions.explanation: Casual 'must': **なきゃ** (short for なければ).
notes: ないじゃ isn't a form.
ないで alone means 'don't (do it)' as a request, the opposite meaning.
なくて alone leaves the sentence unfinished and doesn't mean 'must'.
questions.translation: Oh, it's already 9! I've got to hurry home.

questions.prompt: {会社|かいしゃ}のルールで、{社員|しゃいん}は{全員|ぜんいん}{名札|なふだ}をつけなければ（　）。
questions.explanation: Formal rules: 〜なければ**なりません**.
notes: なければいりません isn't a pattern. いる means 'need'.
なければできません ('can't unless…') is a different meaning.
なければありません isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: Under company rules, all employees must wear name tags.

questions.prompt: {試合|しあい}に{勝|か}つために、{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}しなくては（　）。
notes: なくてはいいです isn't a pattern.
なくてはかまいません isn't a pattern. なくてもかまいません means 'don't have to'.
なくてはください isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: To win the match, we have to practise every day.

questions.prompt: {宿題|しゅくだい}をし（　）はいけません。
questions.explanation: **なくて + は + いけません** = 'must'.
notes: なければは is a double particle and ungrammatical.
なくてもは isn't grammatical.
ないではいけません isn't the obligation pattern.
questions.translation: I have to do my homework.

questions.explanation: Casual 'must': **なくちゃ** (from なくては).
notes: なくじゃ isn't a form. ちゃ comes from ては.
なけちゃ isn't a form.
ないちゃ isn't a form.
questions.translation: It's already 11. I've got to go to bed.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みだから、{早|はや}く{起|お}き（　）いいです。
notes: 起きなかったいい isn't grammatical.
なくてはいい isn't a pattern.
なければいい means 'it's good if you don't', and it misses the 'don't have to' sense.
questions.translation: Tomorrow's a holiday, so I don't have to get up early.

questions.prompt: A：{全部|ぜんぶ}{食|た}べなければいけませんか。　B：いいえ、{全部|ぜんぶ}（　）よ。
options: {食|た}べなければなりません
{食|た}べなくてはいけません
questions.explanation: 'No (you don't have to)': **なくてもいいです**.
notes: なければなりません ('must') contradicts いいえ.
てはいけません means 'must not eat', which is stronger than the question asked.
なくてはいけません means 'must', which contradicts いいえ.
questions.translation: A: Do I have to eat all of it? B: No, you don't have to.

questions.prompt: このアンケートには{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}か（　）かまいません。
questions.explanation: Formal 'don't have to': **なくてもかまいません**.
notes: なければかまいません isn't a pattern.
なくてはかまいません isn't a pattern.
ないでかまいません isn't the standard pattern.
questions.translation: You don't have to write your name on this survey.

questions.prompt: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ（　）{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}きました。
notes: なかった ends a clause and can't connect to the next verb.
ないと ('if you don't') is conditional.
なくて gives a reason ('because I didn't eat…'), but not eating isn't why you went to school.
questions.translation: I went to school without eating breakfast.

questions.prompt: {傘|かさ}を{持|も}た（　）{出|で}かけて、{雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られました。
questions.explanation: Went out **without** an umbrella: 持たないで.
notes: ずで isn't a form. The literary equivalent is ずに.
なくて would make 'not having an umbrella' the reason for going out.
ないて isn't a form.
questions.translation: I went out without an umbrella and got caught in the rain.

questions.prompt: {宿題|しゅくだい}が{終|お}わら（　）、{寝|ね}られませんでした。
questions.explanation: A **reason** ('because it didn't finish') takes **なくて**, not ないで.
notes: なくても ('even if it doesn't finish') is illogical.
なければ ('if it doesn't finish') doesn't fit a past fact.
ないで means 'without doing', but you can't 'not finish' as a manner of sleeping. You need the reason form.
questions.translation: My homework wasn't finished, so I couldn't sleep.

questions.prompt: （Mother to child）もう10{時|じ}よ。{早|はや}く{寝|ね}（　）。
questions.explanation: ます-stem + **なさい** (寝る → 寝なさい).
notes: なさい attaches to the stem (寝), not the dictionary form.
ないさい isn't a form.
なさる is the honorific verb 'to do', not a command ending.
questions.translation: It's already 10. Go to bed now.

questions.prompt: Who would naturally say 「{宿題|しゅくだい}をしなさい」?
options: A shop clerk to a customer
questions.explanation: 〜なさい comes from someone with authority: a parent or teacher.
notes: Ordering your boss around with なさい would be very rude.
Toward a teacher it's far too bossy. Use 〜てください or more polite forms.
Clerks use お〜ください toward customers.

questions.prompt: （Exam instruction）{正|ただ}しいものを{一|ひと}つ{選|えら}び（　）。
questions.explanation: Test instructions use **ます-stem + なさい**.
notes: 選びたい means 'I want to choose'.
選びましょう ('let's choose') isn't the standard exam instruction.
ください needs the て-form (選んでください).
